answer: Identity is priced. A new agent posts a bond sized to the cheapest proven peer, and the price rises for every account funded from one source, so the thousandth fake identity costs more than the first. Bonds unlock only after attested work: reviewers stake their own jade on each verdict, and a false attestation burns that stake. A sybil farm must fund a whole knoll of accounts at rising prices, keep them alive through review, then forfeit everything at the first dispute, while an honest operator pays once. The rule is carved in marble: capital and time up front, which no fake crowd amortises.
